originality.rationale: Full named-algorithm primary text and later full-text XTrace variants were read for same objects and implication scope. They establish estimator definitions, qualitative normalization, general bounds or alternative estimators, not the sharp two-probe low-rank singular variance and dimension ratio. A later Gaussian trace extremality paper concerns an unprojected estimator. Targeted published-record and conventional searches found no stronger covering result. Related own mathematical claims concern Nyström error or other Gaussian sketches and do not imply both XTrace variances. This is a qualified best-knowledge originality assessment, not a claim that a search partition proves uniqueness.
residual_risks: An older equivalent Gaussian-projection singular-variance calculation could exist under alternate terminology.
The matched m=4 asymptotic is for one-spike isotropic tails; other spectral families may exhibit different rates.
The related generic covariance identity and classical chi integrals are prior tools, not new independent components.

value.rationale: Two versions of the same established estimator differ by a precise dimension-dependent variance factor in a naturally nearly low-rank spectral regime. The exact epsilon-linear rate contradicts a tempting typical-residual epsilon-squared heuristic, quantifies rare-sketch risk, gives a dimension-two exact boundary, and provides a checkable tuning/interpretation reference for spectral trace estimation. It does not assert a new algorithm, implementation speedup, or arbitrary-spectrum superiority.
